Welcome back! Stanford let a model write complete viral genomes from scratch and sixteen of them replicate in the lab. Today also covers the fourth AI company to admit its model hacked someone during testing, an empty tab that revealed Google's next enterprise product and an agent that invented people to get its code approved.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Stanford: What happens when an AI writes a whole genome? Meta: Why did four labs miss this for three months? Google: What did an empty tab give away? AISI: Which model created fake humans to win an argument? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Stanford let an AI write a genome from scratch  And do you know what: Sixteen of them work. Researchers used generative models to design complete viral genomes, built them in the lab and watched them replicate.  First time whole genomes have been designed by AI rather than edited or assembled from known parts. The viruses are bacteriophages. They infect specific bacteria and pose no threat to people. The models are Evo1 and Evo2, and the architecture will sound familiar.  They predict the next element in a sequence, the way a language model does. The sequence is genetic code instead of text. The team synthesized 302 designs. Sixteen killed E. coli. A PhD student in the lab watched clear spots appear on the petri dishes in the early hours, the sign the phages were feeding. The medical case is antibiotic resistance. Designing phages rather than hunting for them changes the search entirely. Published in Science with a commentary from the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security.  Their framing is direct: the question is no longer whether generative viral genome design will exist, but whether it can be used without enabling serious harm.  Viruses with disease potential, they write, should not be pursued. Stanford built in constraints. No viruses capable of infecting complex organisms in the training data, phage only, secure lab. Scale matters before anyone extrapolates. This genome runs 5,400 base pairs. The smallest living cell is around 500,000. Humans are three billion. Ahojte lídri,
v poslednej dobe som dostala určitý signál, že osobný vzťah môže byť v
pracovnom prostredí vnímaný ako niečo, čo by mohlo mať vplyv na pracovné
fungovanie.
Keďže nechcem, aby osobné vzťahy akokoľvek ovplyvňovali moju prácu alebo
aby mohli byť vnímané ako niečo, čo by mohlo niekomu v práci uškodiť,
rozhodla som sa nastaviť väčší odstup medzi pracovnou a osobnou rovinou.
Zároveň som sa však zamyslela nad tým, ako som počas posledných rokov
pristupovala k jednotlivým lídrom, a uvedomila som si jednu vec.
Ak som mala k niekomu bližší osobný vzťah, práve voči tomuto človeku som sa
v práci snažila byť ešte dôslednejšia, aby nikdy nevznikol priestor na
pochybnosti, že niekoho zvýhodňujem alebo mu niečo prehliadam.
Ak som napríklad pri kontrole first part checku našla chybu u človeka, ku
ktorému mám osobne bližší vzťah, upozornila som ho na ňu a očakávala som
nápravu. Ak som našla chybu v kódovníku, postupovala som rovnako. V prípade
opakovaných pochybení som informáciu posunula aj koordinátorovi výroby, či
už slovne alebo e-mailom.
Ak som však našla podobné pochybenie u iných lídrov, vo veľa prípadoch som
nápravu vykonala sama bez toho, aby som na chybu konkrétne upozornila.

Odteraz sa budem snažiť ku všetkým lídrom pristupovať rovnako dôsledne, ako
som doteraz pristupovala k človeku, ktorý mi bol osobne bližší.
Ak nájdem chybu v dokumentácii, upozorním Vás na ňu. Ak sa bude pochybenie
opakovať, informáciu posuniem koordinátorovi výroby – nie s cieľom niekomu
spôsobovať problémy alebo ovplyvňovať jeho bonus, ale preto, aby mal o
opakovaných nedostatkoch potrebný prehľad.


V poslednej dobe som ostala prekvapená pri niektorých Vašich first part
checkoch z outputov.
Napríklad pri L6222 sa stretávam so zapísanými hodnotami, pri ktorých mi
nie je jasné, ako mohli vzniknúť, keďže sú uvedené na tri desatinné miesta,
napríklad 9,632°(uhol magnetu) Rovnako pri magnet flux, kde sa objavujú
hodnoty zapísané na tri desatinné miesta. Pri meraní magnet flux rotora z
linky alebo magnetu z outputu by podľa môjho názoru malo byť každému jasné,
aký typ hodnoty a v akej forme má byť do FPCH zapísaný.
Rovnako sa stalo, že na L6221 sa vyrábal model 66H a v dokumentácii boli
zapísané hodnoty pre model 46H.

Líder môže mať veľa práce a môže sa pomýliť. Chyba sa môže stať každému.
Dôležité však je, aby boli údaje vo FPCH reálne a zodpovedali tomu, čo sa
na linke skutočne vyrába a meria.
Prosím preto, aby ste moje upozornenia nevnímali osobne. Nesnažím sa týmto
e-mailom riešiť žiadne osobné vzťahy ani poukazovať na konkrétnych ľudí.
Snažím sa Vám iba priblížiť spô

77077.subject: Helicon Is Live on Testnet: Avalanche’s Biggest Staking and C-Chain Upgrade Since Genesis
77077.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/helicon-is-live-on-testnet-avalanches

Helicon activated on the Fuji Testnet on July 28, 2026, at 11:00 AM ET, bundling six Avalanche Community Proposals into the most significant single upgrade to Avalanche’s staking economics since Genesis. Building on Octane and Granite, it also brought Continuous Execution, formerly known as Streaming Asynchronous Execution, to the C-Chain.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
What’s happening
Helicon shipped six ACPs at once, split across two goals. Four of them, ACP-236, ACP-267, ACP-273, and ACP-285, rework how validators commit capital and get paid. The other two, ACP-194 and ACP-283, rework what the C-Chain can actually do with that validator set.
Staking economics
ACP-236 introduces auto-renewed validator staking. Instead of committing to a fixed end date and manually re-staking every period, validators set a cycle duration and an auto-compound ratio, and the network handles renewal automatically as long as uptime holds.
ACP-273 drops the minimum staking duration from 336 hours (two weeks) down to 48 hours, opening validation to allocators who cannot lock capital for extended periods.
ACP-267 raises the uptime requirement for rewards from 80% to 90%, applying only to validations whose staking period starts on or after Helicon activation. Validations already running when Helicon activates continue to be evaluated against the 80% threshold.
ACP-285 recalibrates the reward curve, lowering the minimum consumption rate from 10% to 7.5% over a 90 day rollout that is now underway, restoring the premium for longer-duration staking that had been flattening over time.
C-Chain execution
ACP-194 decouples consensus from execution on the C-Chain. Blocks are continuously accepted into a queue while a separate executor processes them in parallel, removing the bottleneck created when the two processes had to take turns.
ACP-283 replaces the C-Chain’s fixed 1 wei minimum gas price with a validator-governed floor that adjusts based on real network conditions, closing a spam vector that fixed pricing left open.
Three new P-Chain transaction types make auto-renewed staking work:
AddAutoRenewedValidatorTx registers a validator with a cycle duration and auto-compound ratio instead of a fixed end date.
RewardAutoRenewedValidatorTx is issued automatically by the network at the end of each cycle, requiring no operator signature.
SetAutoRenewedValidatorConfigTx lets an operator update the cycle duration or auto-compound ratio, taking effect only at the next cycle boundary.
Delegations, notably, do not auto-renew and must fit inside a single cycle.
All six ACPs are now live on Fuji. Mainnet activation has not happened yet; that will follow once Fuji has run clean for long enough to verify.
Why it matters
The staking changes solve two real problems at once. Validato
